title: gwf-2006-interbrand

won.source: The Reprobate's own held bio card: "GWF Interbrand Champion (July 16th, 2008 - March 22nd, 2009)" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-the-reprobate.html).

how: Who he won it from, and who took it from him, is not recorded — the bio card states only the dates and the belt's own name.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: Chris O'Malley's own held bio card: won the GWF Championship at Locked N' Loaded 2007, defeating then-champion Michael Toaster (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html).

lost.source: same bio card: lost the title at GWF's Valentine's Vengeance 2008 in a Fatal 4 Way.

how: Lost in a Fatal 4 Way at Valentine's Vengeance 2008 — the other three participants are not named on the surviving record; the belt stayed within his own Cataclysm stable, as stablemate SheltonSplash won it the same night.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: Chris O'Malley's own held bio card: SheltonSplash won "his historic first world's championship reign" the same night O'Malley lost it, at Valentine's Vengeance 2008 (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html).

lost.source: SheltonSplash's own 5 April 2009 promo, "The Living Fairytale," recaps the loss as a flashback with no date given: Don Cicinni beat him with a third Omerta superkick (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html).

how: Lost to Don Cicinni, who needed three Omerta superkicks to keep him down; recovered only as a flashback clip inside a later promo, no date recoverable.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: "20113 — the Final Encounter," the closing show's own main event: a four-corners lumberjack match for the vacant title (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Pinned Robert Garland to become the final GWF Champion, GWF closing for good the same night — the belt goes dark with him still holding it.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: The GWF Hall of Shame's own 28 July 2008 retrospective on the Spirit Squad: "He then became GWF Champion, and went onto become the first Undisputed Champion in GWF History." (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html).

how: No result recorded. The earliest reign the surviving record recovers, presumably preceding Chris O'Malley's own 2007 win, exact placement unrecoverable.

title: gwf-2006-world

lost.source: Chris O'Malley's own held bio card: "Toast had beaten James for the GWF Championship" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html).

how: No result or dates recovered — lost to Michael Toaster at some point before 2007, per a passing line in Chris O'Malley's own bio card.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: Chris O'Malley's own held bio card: "Toast had beaten James for the GWF Championship" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-chris-omalley.html).

lost.source: same bio card: lost the title to Chris O'Malley at Locked N' Loaded 2007.

how: Won from James Murphy, undated; lost to Chris O'Malley at Locked N' Loaded 2007.

title: gwf-2006-world

won.source: SheltonSplash's own 5 April 2009 promo, "The Living Fairytale" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html).

how: How this reign ended is not recorded — the belt is shown vacant, in commissioner Alex Storm's own hands, entering the 20 January 2013 closing show.

title: gwf-2006-intercontinental

won.source: A five-way elimination match for the vacated title (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Outlasted SheltonSplash, Nitro Nick, Jeff Maximus and Ken Davidson to become the belt's own final champion.

title: gwf-2006-intercontinental

won.source: Held as of the 27 March 2009 FNB Reunion show and still held into the January 2013 closing show; no won-date survives (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Voluntarily surrendered the title to SheltonSplash backstage in exchange for a slot in the closing show's own GWF Championship match.

title: gwf-2006-us

won.source: An eight-man reunion-tour tournament final, defeating The Reprobate (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-fnb-reunion-2009-03-27.html).

how: Retained through the fed's own last night, beating The Reprobate a second time in a hardcore defense at 20113, 20 January 2013 (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

title: gwf-2006-tag-team

won.source: "20113 — the Final Encounter" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Beat Neo-Evolution (Kevin McAuliffe and Dave Shadow) to become GWF's final Tag Team Champions.

title: gwf-2006-tag-team

won.source: The GWF Hall of Shame's own 28 July 2008 retrospective on the Spirit Squad: "He and former Spirit Squad opponent JBW formed the Billionaires Club and had a reign as GWF Tag Team Champions." (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/hos-induction-7-28-08.html).

how: No result or date recovered, named only in this one retrospective — likely the belt's earliest reign, given both men's own Spirit Squad-era history.

title: gwf-2006-tag-team

won.source: SheltonSplash's own 5 April 2009 promo, "The Living Fairytale," recaps the loss as a flashback (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html).

how: Lost to XO Malone and Damian DeNiro's own Movement, in a match recorded only as a flashback clip — Damian DeNiro's finisher and interference from a masked ally, Christina Hernandez's manager counterpart on the other stable, are the only surviving detail.

title: gwf-2006-tag-team

won.source: SheltonSplash's own 5 April 2009 promo, "The Living Fairytale" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/rp-the-living-fairytale.html).

how: Billed "The Movement" at the win. How and when this reign ended is not recorded; Numbered Toast held the belts by April 2008.

title: gwf-2006-tag-team
how: Champions as "Numbered Toast" by 27 April 2008, when the pair defended (and kept) the belts at that night's War Games by walking out and padlocking their own opponents inside the cage rather than lose cleanly (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html). By 2013 the belts belonged to Neo-Evolution; how the change happened is not recorded.

title: gwf-2006-tag-team
how: Neo-Evolution's own reign ended in the fed's own last hours, losing to Danny Mainer and Bryan Daniels after a low blow from Danny Mainer's manager, Jessica, turned the match.

title: gwf-2006-international-xtreme
how: Champion as of 27 April 2008, retaining that night in a bloody hardcore defense against Michael Smart (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-sns-2008-04-27.html). How and when the title changed hands afterward is not recorded; Baron Trotter held it by the 2009 reunion tour.

title: gwf-2006-international-xtreme

won.source: Named as champion in the Power 10 column for 27 March 2009 and the SND card for 4 April 2009 (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/power-10-2009-03-27.html; promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-snd-card-2009-04-04.html).

how: A billed 4 April 2009 defense against a returning Mark Madison was never captured with a result. Held the title through the fed's own last night, unifying it with the Co-Cruiserweight Championship in a 20 January 2013 triple threat over XO Malone and Debolt Dragonsbane to become the Undisputed GWF International Xtreme Champion (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

title: gwf-2006-hardcore

won.source: "20113 — the Final Encounter" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Claimed the vacant belt backstage — its previous holder, Jay Ramirez, had been arrested and the title "re-possessed" — after which SheltonSplash made his own already-scheduled tournament bout with Roc Anderson a title match on the spot. Retained, beating Roc Anderson.

title: gwf-2006-hardcore

lost.source: The Reprobate's own held bio card, dated 13 March 2009, already lists this as a "Former Title": "GWF Hardcore Title (???)" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/bio-the-reprobate.html).

how: No result or dates recovered — already a past reign by the time his own bio card was written.

title: gwf-2006-cruiserweight

won.source: "20113 — the Final Encounter" (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: Alex Storm retired the belt and had Debolt Dragonsbane and XO Malone fight for it one last time; Baron Trotter interrupted before either man won it clean, and Storm declared both men Co-Champions on the spot. The lineage was unified into the International Xtreme Championship the same night.

title: gwf-2006-cruiserweight
how: As Toast Hogan, an early gimmick — the GWF Hall of Shame's own 2008 retrospective on the 2006 Food Division craze calls him "a great GWF Cruiserweight Champion." No date or result recovered.

title: gwf-2006-breakthrough

won.source: The Breakthrough Tournament final, a triple threat over Chris Williams and Chris O'Malley (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: The only man ever to hold a title created for one night's own tournament.

title: gwf-2006-sunday-brunch-interbrand

won.source: Named himself the holder from the ring at 20113, 20 January 2013, to argue his own way into the Champion of Champions match (promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html).

how: No prior result survives for this Brunch-program title.

title: gwf-2006-champion-of-champions
label: Michael Smart

won.source: promotions/gwf-2006/archive/show-20113-final-encounter.html

how: Elimination gauntlet among every reigning GWF titleholder present, contested at 20113, 20 January 2013.
